notes: Primary plan. 72 cores per CPU node (Lecture 9). Strong and weak to 288 cores = 4 nodes.
GPU node shape (GPUs and CPU cores per node) unknown until `hpc gpu`; the gpu job is a placeholder shape.
arithmetic: Fixed 100 CG iterations per timed run (runs comparable, core-hours bounded); 3 repeats in one process, report the median; validation runs iterate to a tolerance instead (checks/validate.py).
Strong grids: 2D n=8192 -> N=67,108,864; 3D n=406 -> N=66,923,416. Same work, different stencil and surface/volume.
Memory at 1 rank: N x 8 B = 0.54 GB per vector; classic CG holds 5 vectors (x b r p q) = 2.7 GB, pipelined 8 (x b r p w s z n) = 4.3 GB; fits one node.

Serial time at the strong grid: classic ~96 B/point/iteration (stencil 3 streams, update 6, p update 3) -> 6.4 GB per iteration; at ~10 GB/s for one server core about 0.6 s/iteration, ~1 min per run of 100 iterations, ~3 min with 3 repeats (Mac M5 measured: 1.1 ns/point/iteration, i.e. ~85 GB/s).
Rank counts [1, 2, 4, 9, 18, 36, 72, 144, 288]: up to 288 cores = 4 nodes x 72 (>= 256 required).
Weak scaling: n(P) = round(n0 * P^(1/d)), n0 = 1448 (2D), 128 (3D) -> ~2.1e6 unknowns per rank; at P=288: 2D n=24573 (N=6.04e+08), 3D n=845 (N=6.03e+08); total memory 39 GB (pipelined) over 4 nodes.

Serial sweep: 2D n=[64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192], 3D n=[16, 25, 40, 64, 101, 161, 256, 406]; matrix dimension N from 4.1e3 to 6.7e7 and nonzeros 5N (2D) or 7N (3D), so at each N two nonzero counts are measured.

Iterations-to-tolerance (tol 1e-08) for 2D n=[64, 128, 256, 512, 1024] and 3D n=[16, 25, 40, 64, 101]: CG needs O(n) iterations (cond(A) = cot^2(pi h/2) ~ (2(n+1)/pi)^2), which is why fixed-iteration timing is used for scaling.

Strong/weak series run with two variants: classic CG + blocking halo (baseline) and pipelined CG + overlapped halo (communication hidden). Speedup S = T(1)/T(P), efficiency E = S/P (strong) and T(1)/T(P) (weak), each against the 1-rank run of the same variant.
Variants: full factorial at 72 ranks (1 node) and 288 ranks: 3D 3x2x2 = 12 cells, 2D 2x2x2 = 8 cells, per rank count; 1D slabs of the 3D grid at 288 ranks are 1.4 planes thick.

Layouts per node ['1x72', '2x36', '4x18', '8x9', '72x1'] on 1 and 4 nodes (strong grid, classic+blocking): same cores, fewer ranks -> fewer and larger halo messages and fewer ranks in each MPI_Allreduce.
GPU: strong grids on 1 GPU and on 2 GPUs (2 ranks, one GPU each) of one GPU node; halos go through host buffers (target update), so the 2-GPU run shows that cost.
